channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] Hashim Thaci's second conviction in The Hague reignites debate in Kosovo about justice and the Kosovo Specialist Chambers
item.description: Former President Hashim Thaci has been convicted of trying to influence witnesses in his war crimes trial. The conviction has reignited debate in Kosovo about the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, the court that convicted him.

item.title: [DW] Back to 1997: Russia wants NATO to roll back its eastern expansion
item.description: The Kremlin is reportedly calling on NATO to withdraw from large parts of Eastern Europe. What this would mean for the security of millions of Europeans — and what lies behind Russia's plan.

item.title: [DW] Rights court rules Turkey must release jailed lawmaker Atalay
item.description: The European Court of Human Rights has called for the release of imprisoned elected lawmaker Can Atalay. Atalay has been in prison for almost five years despite rulings from the Turkish Constitutional Court.

item.title: [DW] Students' List candidates take seats as Serbian parliament opens
item.description: Serbia's Student List's candidates have taken their oaths in the inaugural parliament session. As the new majority, they have 90 days to form a government.

item.title: [DW] Putin proposes second humanitarian ceasefire — is it a trap?
item.description: Russian President Putin has suggested evacuating civilians from the embattled Ukrainian city of Kostiantynivka. But experts warn this could serve military, not humanitarian, aims. What should Kyiv do?

item.title: [EU Observer] Italy’s hard definition of antisemitism will shield Israeli crimes and harm free speech
item.description: Italy's Meloni has doubled down on her populist and performative claims to care about Jewish minorities, by imposing a hardline definition of antisemitism that risks gagging debate.

item.title: [EU Observer] UK-EU summit to see mutual love-bombing, but British must decide what to do next
item.description: There will be agreements aplenty in Brussels on Friday, but the UK needs to decide how ambitious its plans for closer integration with the EU will be.

item.title: [EU Observer] Hungary’s new government claws back motorways and tobacco monopoly after years of taxpayer‑funded Orbán luxury travel (Day 191 of the Tisza government)
item.description: Hungary’s new leaders rip up motorway and tobacco deals that once enriched Orbán’s allies, raising the prospect of a massive financial and political reckoning.

item.title: [DW] EU Commission confirms it was targeted in cyberattack using AI tools
item.description: The European Commission was targeted by an "AI-generated cybercampaign," a spokesperson has said. This is the first time the bloc has publicly reported an AI-based cyberattack.

item.title: [DW] Wadephul: 'Coalition of the Willing' talks in Berlin send strong signal to Moscow
item.description: German Foreign Minister Wadephul has said the Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin sends a clear message to Moscow to take peace talks seriously. He also warned Ukraine should be prepared for peace talks to fail.

item.title: [DW] Despite restrictive abortion laws, Poland's 'Abortomat' — a locker that dispenses abortion pills — helps women who want to end a pregnancy
item.description: Abortion laws in Poland are very restrictive. Activists there have found a new way to help women wanting to terminate a pregnancy: the "Abortomat," a locker that dispenses abortion pills. But they face fierce opposition.

item.title: [DW] EU and Indonesia sign trade deal
item.description: A deal covering 730 million people promises lower tariffs and new investment opportunities as the European Union seeks to diversify trade ties amid growing global economic tensions.

item.title: [DW] New EU budget proposal aims at tax gobal tech giants
item.description: European Council President Antonio Costa has proposed a smaller EU budget for 2028-2034, including a 3% tax on major digital firms to ease member states' contributions. France has already rejected the plan as inadequate.

item.title: [Euractiv] Costa proposes shifting €45 billion to farmers
item.description: Money earmarked for rural projects such as roads and tourism would go towards the Common Agricultural Policy

item.title: [DW] Russia strikes Zelenskyy's hometown, killing 2
item.description: The attacks follow Russian President Vladimir Putin's vow of a "painful" response to Ukraine's attacks this week on the Kerch Bridge, linking Russian-occupied Crimea.

item.title: [Euractiv] EU and Indonesia officially sign ‘ambitious’ trade deal
item.description: The agreement includes a dedicated protocol on palm oil

item.title: [Politico Europe] Russian ship damaged by drone attack in Gulf of Finland, Helsinki and Moscow say
item.description: The Finnish coast guard said the ship was known to have ties with Russian armed forces.

item.title: [Euractiv] Finland detects drone attack on Russian cargo ship in Baltic
item.description: The Baltic Sea has become a potential flashpoint in the wake of Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine

item.title: [Financial Times] Navy budget pick has family investments in Trump Jr-linked contractor
item.description: Democrats have promised to raise alleged conflicts of interest concerning administration officials when they take over Congress

item.title: [Financial Times] Traders start to move US copper to China as Trump tariff fears ease
item.description: Acute Chinese shortage and high local premium create lucrative arbitrage

item.title: [Politico Europe] Russian threats ‘less and less hybrid,’ Von der Leyen says after assassination plot in Denmark
item.description: Danish authorities said they thwarted a Russian plan to kill a Ukrainian rapper in September.

item.title: [Euractiv] Costa proposes €204 billion cut to EU budget
item.description: Competitiveness and external action would take deep cuts, while farm and regional funding would be largely spared

item.title: [Politico Europe] Costa cuts proposed EU budget by €44B
item.description: Brussels plans a tax on Big Tech to raise billions for the next budget cycle.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Infographic] Plastics export ban begins: How much more of EU’s 22 million tonne per year trash mountain will go into landfills?
item.description: With record plastic waste and shrinking recycling capacity, Europe’s new export ban risks quietly diverting mountains of rubbish into incinerators, landfills and poorer neighbours’ backyards.

item.title: [EU Observer] COP31 in Antalya: five takeaways from the ‘implementation’ climate summit
item.description: After three decades of UN climate summits, and little progress on climate finance, this year’s meeting (COP31) in Turkey, is likely to be remembered less for what negotiators agreed than for the deals struck on the sidelines.

item.title: [Euractiv] Countries open path towards ‘killer robots’ pact
item.description: Countries agreed to spend two years drafting rules for autonomous weapons, with no guarantee they’ll be legally binding

item.title: [Euractiv] Brits chose Europe once. Can they do it twice?
item.description: Andy Burnham has opened old political wounds and the Brexit number wars

item.title: [Financial Times] The dead hand of history weighs on Deutsche Bank
item.description: Bankers might do well to remember from time to time that they are making decisions that will stick around

item.title: [Financial Times] The manufacturing of novelty
item.description: Polyamory, effective altruism, demand avoidance — a stagnant society is giving new names to old things

item.title: [Financial Times] Oil shipped through Hormuz falls as Iranian strikes increase
item.description: Recovery in Middle Eastern crude exports looks ‘increasingly fragile’, analyst says

item.title: [Financial Times] CVC claims accounting manipulation in €3bn Advent pastry ingredients deal
item.description: US firm denies allegations that Irca’s financial performance was overstated before it agreed to sell Italian business

item.title: [Financial Times] The AI cyber threat is already here
item.description: The freezer war is just a start

item.title: [Financial Times] Russia and Ukraine’s drone war sends optical fibre prices soaring
item.description: Kyiv’s drone advantage is threatened by sixfold price surge in key anti-jamming commodity

item.title: [DW] Ukraine: Zelenskyy says security deal could go to referendum
item.description: The US has broached the idea of Kyiv giving up the Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership, the Ukrainian president said.

item.title: [Financial Times] Nvidia faces US regulator’s probe into its accounting
item.description: Securities and Exchange Commission’s investigation adds to difficulties facing chip group after Jensen Huang’s resignation

item.title: [Financial Times] US tech stocks plunge into bear market in worst week since Covid-19 crisis
item.description: Shares in Anthropic and Nvidia tumble as fears over the AI spending boom grip Wall Street

item.title: [DW] Russian ornithologist jailed over small donations to Navalny's foundation
item.description: Sofia Rosenfeld has devoted her life to studying Arctic birds. A Russian court sentenced her to 3.5 years in a penal colony over donations to Navalny's foundation. Friends and family are fighting for her release.

item.title: [EU Observer] Russian missiles over Poland, European troops in the mud: Ukraine’s defence force is taking shape
item.description: Just hours before the European war games in Poland began, Russian missiles and a drone tore through its Nato airspace.

item.title: [Financial Times] Trump considering new Iran strikes as US military warns of strain on forces
item.description: Officials say indefinite deployments and potential budget cuts risk eroding readiness if conflict continues into the new year

item.title: [Financial Times] Donald Trump threatens ‘tremendous’ tax on data centres built outside US
item.description: President says fight is about preventing Beijing from taking the lead in developing AI technology

item.title: [Politico Europe] UK will take its time setting out Brexit options, says minister
item.description: Hamish Falconer tells POLITICO that discussions around the topic had proved “divisive” and were important to get right.

item.title: [Euractiv] ‘Everyone should leave’: Farage takes Brexit battle back to Brussels
item.description: Farage accused the UK's prime minister of breaking Labour’s pledge not to rejoin the single market

item.title: [Politico Europe] The biggest winners and losers of the EU-UK summit deals
item.description: We take stock of who’s up and who’s down after London and Brussels sign three new deals.

item.title: [Euractiv] Denmark expels Russian diplomat over attempt to kill Ukrainian rapper
item.description: Danish intelligence suspects Moscow of enlisting a local gang to kill Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner during a concert

item.title: [Politico Europe] Andy Burnham discovers nothing in Brussels is ever easy
item.description: Britain’s prime minister is banking on a ‘brainstorm’ to decide Britain’s future with the EU. He just has to get through the spin wars first.

item.title: [Euractiv] Editors’ Choice: Brits back in Brussels
item.description: The Friday edition of our PM newsletter looks at the week that was in European politics and policy

item.title: [Politico Europe] France and Germany complete political deal for ECB leadership
item.description: Paris’ new market-operations portfolio at the European Central Bank could become pivotal in a French debt crisis.

item.title: [EU Observer] Rwanda return hubs may violate EU human rights law, MEPs warn ahead of 2027 deportations
item.description: EU member states are aiming to deport rejected asylum seekers as early as 2027. But many MEPs believe that sending them to Rwanda is illegal as well as wrong.

item.title: [Euractiv] Merz pitches Ukraine investment as opportunity for German firms
item.description: Berlin aims to turn continued financial support into business opportunities for German companies, while Ukraine seeks backing for a €3 billion insurance fund against Russian attacks

item.title: [Politico Europe] Latvian leader calls for closure of EU borders to all Russians
item.description: Andris Kulbergs warned that Europe cannot screen hundreds of thousands of Russian tourists as Moscow escalates its hybrid attacks.

item.title: [Politico Europe] French billionaire hunter takes fight global after California tax defeat
item.description: Gabriel Zucman is rallying politicians in Paris behind his campaign to tax the super-rich. But can he overcome the billionaires and political leaders standing in his way?

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU warns against COP31 becoming a ‘fossil fuel summit’
item.description: The current draft decision text discussed in Antalya would represent "a substantive step backwards" on climate action, European Union leaders said.

item.title: [Euractiv] EU-UK summit falls short of defence industry demands
item.description: There is little in the way of allowing the UK to participate in programmes under the future Competitiveness Fund

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘Fight for our future, not their wars’: youth protests sweep across Europe
item.description: Youth movements took to the streets of Europe's cities on Friday. Organised across the continent, they demand more government spending on education, welfare and action in curbing high housing costs.

item.title: [Euractiv] EU and UK to ‘brainstorm’ future long-term relationship
item.description: 'Life has moved on' since Brexit, the British leader said

item.title: [Euractiv] UK accepts EU food rules with carve-outs
item.description: London secures exemptions on lab-grown meat, animal welfare and pesticides

item.title: [Euractiv] What to watch for in Costa’s EU budget ‘nego box’
item.description: Talk of potential cuts amounting to around €210 billion are making the rounds in Brussels

item.title: [Euractiv] Italian minister says the future of cars is electric
item.description: Gilberto Pichetto Fratin has been a key figure in the fight against an EU combustion-engine ban

item.title: [EU Observer] Russian cruise missiles land in Poland, drones explode over EU diplomats in Kyiv (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,730)
item.description: With bridges shattered, power cut and ships burning off EU coasts, this latest Russian barrage also turns Ukraine’s struggle into a direct test of safety for millions of Europeans and the trade routes they rely on.

item.title: [EU Observer] Burnham hails UK-EU reset on food, carbon markets and youth mobility, after Brexit ‘decade of drift’
item.description: There was plenty of warmth on display at an EU-UK summit in Brussels on Friday. The agreements on carbon emissions, food and youth mobility could form the foundation for a decade of closer EU-UK integration.

item.title: [DW] EU and UK strike 'landmark deal' to strengthen ties after Brexit
item.description: The European Union and the United Kingdom have agreed on "landmark" deals on youth mobility and trade. Leaders on both sides praised the agreement as they seek to rebuild ties.

item.title: [DW] Turkey takes control of opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV
item.description: In the latest in a series of raids and arrests, another major pro-opposition Turkish broadcaster has been brought under state control. This is the third in a year.

item.title: [EU Observer] Estonia’s border closure makes Russia pay a price for alleged arson, as sabotage attacks spread across the EU
item.description: After eight Latvians were caught allegedly trying to burn down an Estonian drone maker, Tallinn’s swiftly decided to close its border with Russia.

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘He who pays the piper calls the tune’: Czech media-freedom attack is part of wider EU malaise, ex-commissioner Věra Jourová says
item.description: Věra Jourová, former values commissioner and vice-president of the EU Commission, warns of the consequences of abolishing licence fees in the Czech Republic, while warning of numerous attacks on media freedom across Europe.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Europe relaxes methane rules while pledging to cut emissions at COP31
item.description: Negotiators from the European Parliament and the 27 EU member states agreed yesterday to postpone some of the rules aimed at cutting methane emissions. This happened while COP31 was still underway, with the EU pledging to reduce emissions globally. Can the EU be trusted to tackle greenhouse gas emissions?

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] Scottish priority is to rejoin the EU after Brexit ‘badly damaged’ UK, Scotland’s Europe minister says
item.description: Scotland, which wants to rejoin the EU and leave the United Kingdom, has pushed for more free movement and less red tape for food and drink exports ahead of a UK-EU summit. Brexit left the UK "badly damaged", Stephen Gethins said.

item.title: [EU Observer] Chinese diplomacy sets lofty goals for a new era
item.description: China’s ambassador to the EU argues that from climate action to digital security, Beijing’s new diplomatic push seeks to bind Europe and the Global South into a growth model that rejects US-style alliances and old Cold War dividing lines.
